newsitem.title: USA: Moisture delays completion of Kansas wheat seeding.
newsitem.headline: Moisture delays completion of Kansas wheat seeding.

text.p: Wet weather during the week ended Sunday prevented producers from completely seeding Kansas's wheat crop, the weekly state crop report said.
The damp conditions prevented further progress and could result in some intended acreage not being planted at all.
Wheat diseases such as stem rust, wheat streak mosaic and septoria continued to be found over much of the state.
Wheat seeding was 99 percent complete, versus 99 last week, 100 a year ago and 99 on average. Wheat was 98 percent emerged, versus 97 last week, 94 last year and 92 on average.
Kansas wheat was rated 89 percent good to excellent, versus 89 percent at that level last week.
Corn was 98 percent harvested versus 97 last week, 99 last year and the average of 96 percent.
Sorghum was 94 percent harvested, versus 86 last week, 99 last year and the average of 98 percent. Soybeans were 94 percent harvested, versus 88 last week, 100 last year and 97 on average.
Pasture condition was rated 69 percent good to excellent, the same as last week.
